Every fiber-adjacent pair has strictly positive coefficient at least c; centered score increments yield exactly the three-term nonnegative remainder. Endpoints and the adjacent-score mass recurrence prove equality rigidity. Log-ratio perturbation bound proves TV control with explicit hypotheses; exact rational perturbation shows deficit \((10/3)\varepsilon^2+O(\varepsilon^4)\), TV \(=|\varepsilon|\). Standalone exact-rational verifier completed 506 cases. Finite verification supplements the universal symbolic proof.

originality.rationale: Ball–Gárgyán 2026 establishes the information and unquantified Blachman–Stam inequality and separately characterizes affine scores. Direct comparison of its Sections 3–5 to the current quantified adjacent-edge remainder and TV estimate found no equivalent or stronger statement. Other discrete scores and continuous analogues do not directly cover this score-specific theorem; remaining possible unindexed reductions are documented.
residual_risks: The 2019 Nishiyama full HTML uses a different Fisher functional; an unrecognized nonlinear equivalence of the two score frameworks cannot be absolutely excluded.
An equivalent adjacent-fiber quantitative estimate might have appeared in old or unindexed conditional-variance/information-stability literature.
The explicit mass-minimum constant is highly nonuniform and probably not best possible; no optimal multiplicative coefficient is claimed.

value.rationale: Unlike nonnegativity or pure equality rigidity, the theorem quantitatively controls two score-curvature energies and their necessary weight match, and upgrades this to explicit total-variation inverse stability for every finite balanced law. A rational perturbation proves local square-root order is necessary. The dependence on minimal masses is openly limiting but still gives a rigorous structural response to near equality in the new information theory.
